notes:
Harmony guest apps now have one stable Dock icon per application and virtual Mac. Keep an icon in the Dock, quit the virtual Mac, then click the icon to start PowerEmu, boot the correct machine, enter Harmony and reopen the guest app. Icons and names remain visible while the VM is off, and quitting an app leaves its pinned icon in place. Guest Applications provides a searchable list instead of a long Dock menu.

Harmony also includes the tested responsiveness, accelerated-window readback, cursor and dual-display stability improvements. Starting a two-screen virtual Mac without a second host display now warns and offers to switch to one screen; saved sessions preserve their original display hardware.

PowerEmu Tools 2.24 is included. Install the update inside each guest to receive the new integration and application reporting. Existing Tools 2.23 installations will be offered the update. This release does not claim to resolve the remaining game-audio distortion or every Harmony rendering issue.

history.notes: Sound in a virtual Mac is better. The emulator now keeps the sound hardware fed while a game is busy, keeps hold of pending audio when this Mac is under load, and follows the buffer size the sound system actually asks for. Games that used to drop out and stall when a new sound started are noticeably cleaner. Crackling on loud effects — a thunderclap, a sudden announcement — has not gone away. A measurement of Warcraft III taken for this release shows why: when a lot of sound has to be mixed at once the callback arrives late, and the card plays a moment that nothing filled. That is the next thing to fix, and it is not fixed here. New: Audio Relay sends this Mac's sound to an old Mac that cannot decode a stream itself. The old Mac keeps the clock and simply reads bytes as its own card calls for them, so a 1.5GHz G4 can play the music and still draw its windows. Also: a virtual Mac now reports its configured processor speed on every CPU, including older configurations, and guest clock connections are reused rather than remade.

A virtual Mac can now be given a second screen. With two displays each guest screen gets its own window; with one they stand side by side in a single window. Harmony spans both, so a guest window can be dragged from one of this Mac's screens to the other, and the guest's second screen is matched to the display showing it so its windows come out the right size rather than half size on a Retina display. The second guest screen has no 3D acceleration - there is one accelerated card, so OpenGL games have to run on the first screen. The performance overlay now shows a panel on each screen, each reading its own card, with a light style that shows just the frame rate and the processor. Also new: snapshots with rollback, duplicating a machine, reclaiming its disk space and running it isolated from the network; printing to a printer the guest already knows how to talk to; the microphone; opening a file from this Mac in the virtual Mac; and a USB device that is remembered and taken at every start. PowerEmu Tools 2.23 is included - update it inside the virtual Mac so Harmony can match the second screen. Fixes: a display pitch the guest could ask for would stop the emulator; the hardware cursor works with two screens; Command-W reaches the guest.

The guest's picture is drawn at the display's own scale, so it is sharper on Retina screens; Sharp, whole pixels now rounds to whole screen pixels rather than whole points. A new Picture setting beside Scaling in the toolbar fits, fills or stretches the guest's screen. Display filters now apply instead of doing nothing. Going full screen with Harmony on no longer leaves a black window with no way back. A guest application's icon leaves this Mac's Dock as soon as it quits. A virtual Mac lent an external disk that is no longer connected now starts without it, rather than refusing to start because another disk has taken its device name.
Fixes the four-CPU option, which could not start a virtual Mac in 0.3.3: the emulator it shipped with still allowed only two.

The Apple logo no longer shears at startup on displays whose width is not a multiple of 64. A virtual Mac can now be given four CPUs, which is experimental, and 32-bit guests run them in parallel. A virtual Mac whose inserted disc has since been deleted now starts with an empty drive instead of refusing to start.

Harmony's "could not match the display" notice can be dismissed now — it goes on the first click or key, and says whether the tools need installing or the virtual Mac ended up at a different size. Display filters and scaling choices for the guest's screen, in the window's toolbar. US English throughout. Set up a virtual Mac from a Mac OS 8 or 9 install disc. A dual-processor Power Mac now really has two processors, as About This Mac already claimed.

Guest applications in the Dock now open properly, stay put while you work, and clear themselves when the virtual Mac stops. Fullscreen starts below the notch on Macs that have one, and the startup resolution can be chosen in Display.

Adds Harmony window integration for Tiger and Leopard, including host/guest window stacking, menu and Dock integration, modal sheets, minimize and restore, and file drag-and-drop in both directions. Adds native PowerEmu Tools install and uninstall packages, configuration tabs, VM reordering, larger Leopard VRAM support, and an experimental two-CPU option. This release continues to use Radeon 9200 graphics.
